Alex — thanks, appreciate the clear checklist. High level reply now; technical attachments + checklist to follow before EOD Wednesday.

Plan (summary):
1) Primary transport: HTTPS HEC endpoint with optional syslog over TLS for legacy collectors. HEC gives better parsing & batching controls which reduces cost and preserves schema.
2) Schema: JSONL events with a small required header (timestamp, service, level, trace_id) and an extensible payload. We will provide a sample schema file and a minimal acceptance JSONL sample.
3) Auth: mTLS recommended for on-prem forwarder to VPC-edge. Token header option (short-lived) available for partners with constrained PKI. We will provide certificate rotation guidance and an automated renewal script (example).
4) PII: Redwood does not perform automatic PII redaction inside the customer enclave by default. We can offer a pre-forward redact step as a professional services engagement or ship a slim filter (configurable regex/hash) to run in the forwarder. Please confirm preference.

We'll attach: redwood_siem_onramp_spec.pdf (technical), tracehook_header_examples.txt, and a delivery SLA workbook. Meeting: I've provisionally scheduled a 30m tech handoff Thu 14 May 09:00 PT — Cal invite will come via Marissa (cc).

Summary (technical):
- Transport: HTTPS HEC endpoint (recommended). Supports gzip and chunked ingestion. Syslog over TLS (RFC5425) supported as fallback; recommend HEC for structured events and lower parsing overhead.
- Porting & firewall: outbound to edge.redwood-inference.net:443 (HEC) / 6514 (syslog-tls). We support IP allowlist ranges per customer (we'll provide list at onboarding).
- Schema (minimal fields):
  - timestamp (ISO8601)
  - service (string)
  - level (string: DEBUG/INFO/WARN/ERROR)
  - event_id (uuid)
  - trace_id (hex)
  - host (fqdn)
  - message (string)
  - payload (object, optional)
Sample JSONL line attached in tracehook_header_examples.txt.
- Authentication: mTLS with x.509 certs minted by customer's internal PKI or Redwood-managed intermediate (customer choice). Cert rotation: recommend 90d rotation; we provide a rotation helper tool that performs staged rollout and key rollover with no ingestion downtime. Token header: X-Redwood-Auth: <short-lived-jwt> available for restricted setups, rotating every 24h.
- PII handling: By default we do not alter customer data. For customers who request pre-forward redaction we can deploy a filter in the forwarder (configurable: regex, field-based hashing, or custom scrub rules). This is an optional service.
- Evidence & audit bundle: We generate a compressed evidence packet on request (logs + trace correlation samples + delivery receipts) with configurable retention policy. For legal hold we can keep a snapshot for 180 days under a secure S3 with KMS; longer retention possible under contract.

Attachment: redwood_siem_onramp_spec.pdf contains a mapping table for field names -> Splunk/Elastic/QRadar examples and an HEC endpoint handshake sequence.

Happy to review these live on Thu.

-Kim

SecOps team — quick answers inline. Quoting your questions above.

- PII redaction: Redwood will not unilaterally mutate customer events. We will ship a pre-forward filter package (OSS-based, configurable) that runs in the forwarder inside your environment. Defaults: mask SSN-like patterns, hash email local-parts, and provide an allowlist to opt-in fields. False positive rate depends on rules; we'll share test harness results and a sample FP rate <0.3% for standard regex filters. If you require hard drop on high-risk matches, we can enable a policy to drop instead of mask.

- Trace correlation & timestamps: the forwarder preserves trace_id and timestamp as received. Redwood runtime does not rewrite trace_id. We will persist event timestamps as-is and attach an ingestion_received timestamp at the edge; delta is recorded in metadata, not used to overwrite original timestamp. We support millisecond precision (ISO8601 with ms) end-to-end.

- Signed manifests: yes. We produce a signed daily manifest (SHA256) and an RSA-signed receipt for the compressed evidence bundle. We can integrate automated artifact delivery to your S3 or provide an on-demand bundle via a secure transfer.

Mutual action plan (agreed next steps):
1) Thu 14 May 09:00 PT — tech handoff (calendar invite live).
2) By Wed 20 May — we deliver sample JSONL stream + redaction test harness for your team to run.
3) By Fri 22 May — security + procurement sign-off (target).
4) Post-sign: 2-week onboarding window for forwarder installation + smoke tests.
